Subject: Propulsion demo: engine slate, cost/latency tradeoffs, next steps

Hi Alex / Jamie —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the model slate we recommend for Propulsion Analytics based on the demo signals and your latency/cost constraints. I attached the benchmark CSV, prompt pack, and a pricing workbook for visibility.

Topline recommendation (shortlist of candidates):

1) Redwood-XL-13B (int8 / quantized) — balanced
- Quality: High on instruction-following and low hallucination in our tests for your Q/A flows (see prompts "propulsion_fin_qna" in the prompt pack).
- Latency: ~120–180ms p95 on a single A100 equivalent with batching=4 in our config.
- Cost: Estimated unit cost in pricing_workbook tab '13B-quant' — lowest of the high-quality options.
- When to use: primary model for customer-facing summarization and answer generation.

2) Mistral-Instruct-7B (int8) — low cost, fast
- Quality: Strong for short-form completions and routing; struggles a bit on long-form financial reasoning (we saw drop in factual recall in the benchmark CSV).
- Latency: ~70–110ms p95.
- Cost: Lowest per-token cost; good for pre-filtering and low-risk outputs.
- When to use: candidate for ingestion/assistant routing and cheap inference paths.

3) Llama2-70B (q4hf) — high quality fallback
- Quality: Best factuality on the multi-turn tests; better on heavy-context prompts in our evals.
- Latency: ~400–600ms p95 if run non-sharded; recommend dedicated capacity and request-level caching for hot prefixes.
- Cost: Highest per-token; best reserved for SLAs or complex explanation tasks.
- When to use: escalation path for regulated responses or when higher quality is required.

Operational and safety notes:
- We suggest prefix caching on common prompts and a lightweight reranker (Mistral as cheap filter + Redwood-XL for final output) to balance cost + quality.
- Prompt-based hallucination checks included in prompt_pack_v1 (simple QA checks and veracity probes).
- If Propulsion needs structured outputs (CSV/JSON response), Redwood-XL produced the most predictable parseable outputs during tests.

Attachments:
- propulsion_benchmarks_20280410.csv (benchmarks by prompt sets)
- propulsion_prompt_pack_v1.zip (prompt templates, test set descriptions)
- redwood_pricing_workbook.xlsx (unit-cost scenarios for hosted vs. dedicated)

Next steps / asks:
1) Can you confirm the top two priority use-cases (you said: automated investment summaries + customer-facing Q/A)?
2) Share a representative test dataset (redacted) we can run through the short-list for a freeze-frame eval.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra lead — proposed times Wed/Thu next week.

If you want, we can also propose an A/B plan for the first two weeks of the pilot (Mistral routing + Redwood-XL final vs Redwood-XL-only) to track cost & quality.

Thanks,
Hannah

Alex — quick answers, from ops + procurement perspective: 

1) Hallucination controls / veracity probes
- See folder 'prompt_pack_v1/veracity_checks' (Drive link in the deck). The two key probes we ran:
  a) Entity presence check (does model return exact ticker symbol from context?)
  b) Source citation probe (model asked to list source id + confidence score).
- We recommend running both against a 200-record sample of your KB. If you want, Redwood can run that sample as an objective eval (we'll return a short report).

2) Hosted VPC vs Dedicated for Llama2-70B
- If you need strict data residency and minimal egress, Redwood Dedicated is the safest path. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and private networking; we'll also enable key-management integration (KMS/HSM) for encryption-at-rest.
- Hosted VPC can be ok for faster time-to-value if your compliance team allows a managed plane with VPC peering; it is cheaper to start but less isolated.

3) Guardrail / rollout suggestion
- Phase 0: run both Redwood-XL-13B and Mistral-7B in parallel on a small traffic slice (5–10%) to get production delta on hallucination rates and latency.
- Phase 1: promote Redwood-XL-13B as 60% traffic, Mistral 30%, Llama2-70B 10% (fallback). Collect a weekly regression report.

4) Logistics
- Thu 12 Apr 2028 10:00am PT works for us for the deep-dive. I'll include the short evaluation checklist and an agenda (15-min infra q’s, 30-min model tradeoffs, 15-min ops/next steps).
